items.evidence: Notes cover the wheel sensor cost ('Wheel sensor 50x push button cost', 'Budget max €12 per remote') but never mention voice/speech recognition or the Industrial Designer's components presentation (chip, push buttons). Transcript shows the User Interface Designer, not the Industrial Designer, raised the voice recognition chip email.
Notes never say the UI Designer presented existing remote controls from the web; only the plastic cover debate from that talk appears.
Nothing about dropping the extra buttons of the existing models to make the design simpler and more ergonomic; 'Simple remote interface confirmed' refers to the prior meeting's recap.

'Fancy look prioritized over function', 'Trend toward fruit/vegetable shapes', 'Spongy material trend noted' cover the trends, but the notes do not say the Marketing Expert presented them or mention the fashion watchers / ranking of fancy, innovative, easy to use.
'Trend toward fruit/vegetable shapes', 'Spongy material trend noted', and the banana shape and spongy case appear as design items.
'Design Decisions' section lists the features settled (wheel, buttons, lighting, banana shape).
Notes have banana shape, yellow color, spongy cover and 'Lighted buttons', but not the wheel on top, the standard chip or standard battery, or dropping speech recognition.
'Industrial and UI designers to collaborate on prototype' and 'Prototype evaluation planned to check user requirements fit'.
'Industrial and UI designers to collaborate on prototype (22:55)'.
'Prototype evaluation planned to check user requirements fit (22:55)'.
'Design Decisions' section lists the agreed features.

'Banana shape proposed for remote', 'Yellow color matches company scheme', spongy cover appears only as 'Spongy material for case questioned' and a 'spongy cover suggested'; framed as proposed/questioned rather than decided.

'Wheel seen as easy and innovative', 'Potential competitive advantage', 'Wheel control included', but the notes never state the decision to keep it despite the higher cost; they still list 'Need discussion on wheel necessity'.
Notes do not say the wheel goes on the top; only 'Ergonomic curve for wheel and buttons'.
No mention of the standard chip or of leaving out speech recognition.

errors.claim: Heart-shaped core with spongy cover suggested
errors.why_wrong: Project Manager said 'something odd shaped, with a spongy cover'; nothing heart-shaped was mentioned.

errors.claim: Industrial Designer: Assess cost implications of wheel sensor
errors.why_wrong: No one assigned this; the group decided to keep the wheel even if the cost is higher.

errors.claim: Project Manager: Facilitate discussion on wheel sensor necessity
errors.why_wrong: The wheel question was settled in the meeting (kept); no follow-up discussion was assigned.

errors.claim: Industrial Designer: Develop banana-shaped spongy case design
errors.why_wrong: Project Manager asked the Industrial Designer and UI Designer to work together on the look and feel and prototype; no separate case-design task was given to the Industrial Designer.
The banana shape was agreed ('Maybe we can keep the banana', later 'we have uh this banana shape... So the colour is yellow'), not just proposed.
